blogs.title: Breaking the Rules: When TAVI is the Only Option for Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis
blogs.description: The ESC guidelines clearly favor surgical intervention for prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE). However, in patients with prohibitive surgical risk and complex comorbidities, clinicians often face a 'no-win' scenario. This post explores the clinical reasoning and multidisciplinary decision-making required to justify a transcatheter approach in a 'forbidden' territory, focusing on the transition from infection resolution to managing structural valve deterioration.

blogs.title: The Nesting Doll Challenge: Navigating TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV Anatomy
blogs.description: As TAVI becomes the standard of care, we are increasingly seeing 'nesting doll' scenarios of serial reinterventions. This post dives into the 'archaeology' of the aortic root, discussing how to use multislice CT (MSCT) and 3D modeling to map out previous valve frames, assess coronary ostial heights, and predict the interaction between multiple overlapping stents to ensure a safe landing zone.

blogs.title: Maximizing the Orifice: Strategies to Overcome Patient-Prosthesis Mismatch in Triple-Stented Valves
blogs.description: With each successive valve added, the effective orifice area (EOA) shrinks, raising the risk of severe patient-prosthesis mismatch (PPM). This post analyzes the specific procedural strategies used in this case—including high implantation depth to prevent leaflet folding and high-pressure balloon post-dilation—to optimize hemodynamics in a severely restricted, triple-stented anatomy.

blogs.title: Running Out of Space: The Limits of Serial TAV-in-TAV Interventions
blogs.description: What happens when the third valve fails? This post discusses the 'end-game' of transcatheter valve therapy. We will consider the long-term implications of cumulative mesh burden on coronary access and explore emerging, high-risk maneuvers like bioprosthetic valve fracture or intentional leaflet laceration (e.g., BASILICA) as potential last-resort strategies for patients with exhausted anatomical real estate.
